content.text: Missing invariant bounding `i` (j < i < v.Length) in mlastMaximum.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "In mlastMaximum the loop invariants say nothing about the range of i (the invariant 0<=i<v.Length present in mmaximum2 is missing). Since i is a loop target, after any iteration Dafny knows nothing about i, so v[i] in the invariants and loop body may be out of range, and the postcondition 0<=i<v.Length cannot be established. Adding invariant j<i<v.Length (which holds initially with i=v.Length-1, j=v.Length-2, and is preserved since i is either kept or set to the old j) fixes it."}
EOF
sed -i '68a\    invariant j<i<v.Length' program.dfy && sed -n 64,76p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
I fixed it, and `dafny verify program.dfy` now reports 12 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the loop in `mlastMaximum` was missing an invariant that keeps `i` in range. The similar loop in `mmaximum2` has `0<=i<v.Length`, but this one didn't. The loop body changes `i`, so after an iteration Dafny no longer knew anything about its value. That caused all five errors: `v[i]` could be out of range in the invariants and the loop body, and the postcondition `0<=i<v.Length` couldn't be proved.

**Fix:** I added one invariant at line 69 of `program.dfy`:
```dafny
invariant j<i<v.Length
```
It holds when the loop starts, because `i = v.Length-1` and `j = v.Length-2`. Each pass either leaves `i` alone or sets it to the current `j`, and then `j` goes down by one, so `j < i` still holds. When the loop exits, `j == -1`, which gives `0 <= i < v.Length`.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before editing, classifying the failure as an invariant / preservation problem.
